summary: 1955 10x10 ground house on English Peak in the Marble Mountain Wilderness; NHLR-registered 1994; staffed until 1973; volunteers restored it in 1996 and maintained it in 2024.

facts.design: 10 by 10 foot ground house built in 1955; earlier fire spotters used the rock outcrop with a magneto telephone

access.note: Hike-in in the Marble Mountain Wilderness; no source read says whether the house is open to visitors

visit.trail_note: About 14 miles and 5,300 feet of climbing from Little North Fork Campground (SummitPost)

events.note: 10 by 10 foot ground house; NHLR and the 2024 FFLA reshare both give 1955
Tom Taylor cabin, the lookout's living quarters, rebuilt per NHLR; SummitPost dates the present structure to the 1940s
Ranger Everett Jansen's account describes construction of the English Peak Cabin in 1942; assumed to be the same cabin as the Tom Taylor Cabin
Restored by volunteers after falling into disrepair
Volunteer family built, painted and installed new shutters; the FFLA reshare is dated October 15, 2024

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the Tom Taylor Cabin was rebuilt in 1940, SummitPost says the present structure dates to the 1940s, and a 1942 ranger account describes building the English Peak Cabin that year. The three dates are not reconciled, so the story says the sources give different dates and lists each one. The 1942 account is assumed to describe the same cabin.

notes_for_editor: Staffing 'unstaffed' as of 1973 is inferred from SummitPost's last staffing year; no later staffing source was found. Whether the house is open to visitors is not stated in any source read. The Klamath NF Facebook post returned a login wall and was not used; the 2024 details come from the FFLA Instagram reshare. The Redding and Bluewater articles were blocked (403) and not used. The brief's 'access unknown' is replaced with 'public' (hike-in).
